scenes.title: 보이는 칼과 맞았다는 판정
lines: An attack pose must communicate where and when it hits. If the motion looks right but the result surprises us, the controls can feel wrong. We'll align the weapon's visible path, its collision region and the pose that registers on contact. The region that tests whether an attack reaches its target is a hitbox. The part of a character that can receive that attack is a hurtbox. The game can register a hit when those regions meet the right conditions. The visible sword model and the region that tests for contact serve different purposes. A tiny region fitted too tightly to a fast blade can miss where the player expects contact. Adjust the attack's reach so the result makes sense in play. We'll keep the sword and swing fixed and change only the collision range. A larger region isn't automatically better. Players need to understand the relationship between the visible hit and its result.

scenes.title: 옆에서 겹쳐 보여도 실제 경로는 다를 수 있다
lines: Tuning the size is different from putting the attack in the wrong place. From the side, blade and opponent can overlap even if the blade passes in front of or behind the target. One flattering camera angle can hide the difference. Our grid marks the reference plane for attacker and target. The play camera and overhead camera show the same instant. First the tip misses the path. Turn the body and adjust the arm so the blade crosses the target. Moving only the hitbox could make the attack connect. But a reaction to a blade that visibly passes somewhere else is harder to read. Distinguish a little extra reach from correcting a misplaced movement. The visible path and collision should describe the same action.

scenes.title: 어느 자세에서 맞게 할 것인가
lines: Once the path is right, choose when the attack can hit. It may not deal damage the whole time the arm moves. Frames in which the attack can register are called active frames. The hand close to the body and the fully extended arm create different impressions. A brief pause on impact, called hit stop, makes that pose especially noticeable. Activating the hitbox helps determine the impact pose the player sees. We'll move only the active window within the same swing. Compare the poses at contact, then watch them at normal speed. The attack needn't become active as soon as the swing begins. It can connect later at a clearer pose. Both position and timing must make sense alongside the visible action.

scenes.title: 동작과 판정을 따로 완성하지 않기
lines: Leaving collision until the animation is finished can mean substantial rework. Animators who consider contact and gameplay designers who examine the pose can shape a more coherent hit. Return to the first attack. Slightly adjusted reach, a path through the opponent and an active window on a strong pose work together. A beautiful attack and a convincing hit belong to the same action. The controls feel clear when both the image and the rules communicate that action.
